Data Scientist and ML EngineerData engineers prepare inputs, data scientists develop models and ML engineers operate predictions

The original workflow separates data preparation, model development and serving

An End-to-End ML WorkflowOne end-to-end workflow connects the roles introduced on the previous slide

The same workflow becomes one end-to-end responsibility

Training and InferenceTraining updates model weights from labeled examples; inference uses the saved weights

Training changes weights; inference applies the learned weights to new inputs

ML PipelineFeature engineering computes model inputs, then training fits and evaluation checks a model

Raw data passes through feature engineering, training and evaluation

ML Pipelines at ScaleFeature, training and inference pipelines may run separately and share versioned assets

Feature, training and inference pipelines can run on different schedules

Data Stores and ML InfrastructureOperational records become analytical data and reusable inputs for training and prediction

Operational data, analytical storage and ML infrastructure serve different roles

ML Pipeline StagesData sources, features, training and inference form separate stages

One feature store connects feature, training and inference pipelines

Fraud Detection DataThe fraud label is the outcome; transactions, profiles and card records supply candidate inputs

Fraud prediction combines transactions, profiles and credit-card details

Source Tables and Update RatesDifferent update rates explain why every feature need not be recomputed together

Transaction, card and profile tables are refreshed at different rates

Keys and JoinsKeys identify records and connect tables, but time boundaries still control eligible values

Primary keys identify rows and join keys connect the three source tables

One Big TableEach row represents one transaction; features are inputs and fraud is the target label

One prediction row combines keys, event time, features and a label

Four-Hour Transaction FeaturesGroup recent transactions by card, then calculate the four-hour aggregates shown below

A four-hour window summarizes recent transactions for each credit card

Features at the Prediction TimeHistorical training rows must use only information available at their prediction time

Shared features still need an explicit time boundary for each prediction

Training, Validation and TestTraining fits weights, validation selects candidates and test data checks the final choice

Training fits parameters, validation selects candidates and test checks the final choice

Iterative Model TrainingUse validation to improve candidates while keeping the test set outside the tuning loop

The validation loop improves a model while the test set remains separate

Training Code and EvaluationOriginal two-way code example; model selection still needs a separate validation step

The original code fits a classifier and reports its predictions on held-out data

Model Development LoopsArchitecture, hyperparameters and fitted weights are changed at different iteration levels

Architecture, hyperparameters, training and evaluation form nested iteration loops

Batch InferenceA scheduled job transforms many records, predicts outcomes and stores the results

Batch inference writes predictions that applications can read later

Online InferenceA request triggers preprocessing and prediction before a result returns to the application

Online inference transforms a request and returns a model prediction

Real-Time Features and ServingPrecomputed and on-demand features can be combined to satisfy a prediction request

Model serving combines request features with precomputed online features

A Real-Time ML ArchitectureRead the transformer as preprocessing, then follow the predictor and the feature-store lookup

The serving path connects the predictor, transformer and online feature store

§ 01 · DevOps for Code

01

DevOps for Code

version, test and release code with Git and Jenkins

02

MLOps for Data and Models

add data and models to the same loop

DevOpsDevOps joins development and operations through versioned code and automated delivery

Git tracks code versions and Jenkins runs build, test and deployment jobs

Version Control with GitGit records each code change as a commit that can be compared, shared and restored

Every change reaches the shared repository as a recorded commit

Branches and Pull RequestsWork happens on a branch and merges into main only after review and tests

Pull requests are where code review and CI meet

Jenkins and CI/CDJenkins is an open-source automation server for build, test and deployment pipelines

Git records code changes and Jenkins executes the configured pipeline

JenkinsfileA pipeline is a versioned recipe for commands that run on the selected agent

Add build, package and deploy stages with the commands your project needs

Release and RecoveryTrack the running version and prepare a recovery path for unhealthy releases

Versioned artifacts and production signals make release decisions traceable

§ 02 · MLOps for Data and Models

01

DevOps for Code

version, test and release code with Git and Jenkins

02

MLOps for Data and Models

add data and models to the same loop

Why ML Systems Keep ChangingA fixed model can become less useful when its inputs or target relationships change

Inputs and targets can change after a model is deployed

MLOpsMLOps connects ML development to repeated validation, deployment and monitoring

MLOps connects a working ML system to repeated validation and improvement

DevOps and MLOpsML adds changing data and learned models to the software change-and-test path

MLOps must check changes in incoming data as well as changes in code

Reproducible MLTrace a deployed model back through its data, feature definitions and training process

Reproduction requires linked versions of data, feature definitions, code and models

Data Versioning with GitDVC (Data Version Control) tracks external data references in this 2025 tool comparison

Data versions need recoverable content and references alongside the code version

Model Development and ReleaseUse common held-out evaluation conditions and explicit bias checks when reading this checklist

A candidate is compared with the deployed model before release

Development and Main BranchesBranches and review gates separate experimentation, validation and production release

Development and release paths keep training data and evaluation results together

Staged Model Release and RollbackCheck a candidate in service before sending all production traffic to it

Release decisions use evidence collected at increasing levels of exposure

Tests in ML SystemsPlace checks at the data, feature, training, API and monitoring boundaries

Tests cover data, feature code, models, APIs and running predictions

Feature and Model TestsTest feature computations and model behavior before relying on their outputs

Feature checks and model checks answer different failure questions

CI, CD and Continuous TrainingMLOps extends software delivery with data checks and controlled model updates

Automated execution still needs an explicit decision before production changes

Feature and Prediction LogsLog the model version, input features, prediction and identifiers needed to find later outcomes

Feature and prediction logs reconnect source inputs, serving and later training

Use Case: Data DriftCompare pipeline inputs, serving inputs, labels and their relationships at the marked locations

Pipeline inputs, serving inputs, labels and outcomes can change in different places

Drift TypesConcept drift changes P(Y | X). Prediction error alone does not establish concept drift

Different drift signals require different checks before a model update

MLOps Tools by StageEach stage of the ML lifecycle has its own representative tools

DevOps tools manage code; MLOps tools add data, experiments and models

Experiment Tracking with MLflowEach run records the parameters, metrics and model of one training attempt

Code goes to Git; runs, metrics and models go to the tracking server

Managed MLOps PlatformsCloud providers bundle the same stages into one managed service

Open-source stacks trade setup work for flexibility

Takeaway: ML Systems

2DevOps versions code with Git and automates build, test and release
3MLOps adds data versions, model releases, tests and drift monitoring to that loop
